harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Deployed a simple inventory web application on node1 (CentOS Stream 10), served by httpd on TCP port 8181, while keeping SELinux in enforcing mode. Fixed the SELinux port labeling gap (8181 was not in http_port_t) with `semanage port -a -t http_port_t -p tcp 8181`, opened the firewalld port, verified the app serves HTTP 200, then performed the mandatory single-node restart and confirmed the boot ID changed and all state (SELinux enforcing, httpd active, port context, firewall rule, app content) recovered cleanly.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 OS/SELinux status and confirmed no pre-existing inventory app (getenforce=Enforcing, no /opt,/srv content)
Installed httpd and policycoreutils-python-utils via dnf
Created inventory app at /var/www/inventory/index.html (auto-labeled httpd_sys_content_t)
Created /etc/httpd/conf.d/inventory.conf with Listen 8181 and VirtualHost
Started httpd and observed bind failure on 8181 (Permission denied) confirming SELinux was blocking the non-standard port while still enforcing
Added SELinux port context: semanage port -a -t http_port_t -p tcp 8181
Restarted httpd; confirmed active, listening on 8181, SELinux still Enforcing
Verified app via curl to $NODE_IP:8181 returning HTTP 200 with inventory content
Opened firewalld port 8181/tcp permanently and reloaded
Captured pre-restart baseline: boot_id, getenforce, httpd active, curl 200
Restarted node1 via systemctl reboot (backgrounded to return ack before disconnect)
Polled node1 until exec succeeded again, confirming reconnection
Verified boot_id changed (71f12f87... -> 383d9e44...) proving actual restart
Verified post-restart recovery: SELinux Enforcing, httpd active+enabled, firewalld port persisted, SELinux http_port_t includes 8181, curl to app returns HTTP 200 with correct content

evidence.requirement: Inventory app served over TCP 8181 on node1
evidence.summary: Created app content and vhost config, httpd active and listening on *:8181, curl returns HTTP 200 with inventory HTML

evidence.requirement: SELinux mandatory access control remains enforcing throughout
evidence.summary: getenforce/sestatus show Enforcing before, during, and after the fix and restart

evidence.requirement: Proof SELinux was actually the enforcing control (not bypassed) for the non-standard port
evidence.summary: httpd failed to bind 8181 with Permission denied while 8181 was absent from http_port_t; after semanage port -a adding 8181 to http_port_t, bind succeeded
firewalld initially lacked port 8181; opened and reloaded permanently; confirmed present after reboot
Captured boot_id 71f12f87-337d-4ff3-b414-9680244c2694, SELinux Enforcing, httpd active, curl HTTP 200

evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledgement returned before disconnect
evidence.summary: Backgrounded systemctl reboot returned 'reboot-scheduled' acknowledgement immediately

evidence.requirement: node1 restart actually occurred (changed boot identity) and node became reachable again
evidence.summary: Node connection dropped/timed out across several polls, then exec succeeded again; new boot_id 383d9e44-a321-4a71-8a48-9acab6a5754f differs from baseline, proving an actual reboot occurred

evidence.requirement: node1 post-restart recovery of required services/data and SELinux state
evidence.summary: After reboot: SELinux Enforcing, httpd active+enabled, listening on 8181, SELinux port context and firewalld rule persisted, curl returns HTTP 200 with correct inventory content
